exceptions.reason: The Schmitt-trigger op-amp uses strict=false, so its saturation branches are event relations and the rectangle output may only switch when V0*v_in crosses a supply limit. For R1=1000, R2=1500, Vps=15 and V0=15000 that crossing is at |vOutTriangle| = (Vps*R1 - (R1+R2)*Vps/V0)/R2 = 9.998333 V, so the ideal circuit is strictly periodic. Rumoca switches at exactly that amplitude every half period at both 1e-6 and 1e-10. The default OMC reference switches early and irregularly (amplitudes from 1.886 V to 9.994 V, half periods from 0.0237 s to 0.0498 s), so its phase drifts and 47 of 66 channels deviate. OMC at 1e-10 moves toward the analytic amplitude but still switches irregularly, and OMC at 1e-12 does not finish within 600 s, so there is no converged reference. This is a reference-generation failure, not strict-high credit.
